https://www.politico.eu/article/moscow-s.text: Russia will intensify its attacks on military and industrial facilities in Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine, Moscow announced Sunday. Writing on Telegram, Russia’s Defense Ministry said , “Strikes by the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation against military and military-industrial facilities, as well as related infrastructure in Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine, will be intensified.” The threat came following Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s statement that Kyiv would respond to Russian attacks by targeting the country’s oil refineries. Advertisement Advertisement “The people of Ukraine should blame only the head of the Kyiv regime for this,” the Russian Defense Ministry stated, referring to the Ukrainian president. “It is Zelenskyy who bears full personal and political responsibility for this.” In an interview with Reuters , Zelenskyy said Saturday that Ukrainian forces “have to respond in any way we can” to Russian attacks, which are increasingly targeting bridges across the Dnipro River in the capital. “With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners: what gives money to them for this war,” he added, while saying Ukraine would not retaliate by deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. The Russian government also accused Kyiv of attempts “to disrupt voting in the elections … through terrorist strikes on civilian targets on Russian territory.” President Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party largely dominated the results of Russia’s legislative elections, held from Sept. 18 to 20. Russia’s threat to intensify strikes on Ukraine came on the same day as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise one-day visit to Kyiv in a show of support to Ukraine. During Merz’s visit, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that Russia had struck the roadway of the North Bridge in the city. On Saturday, Russia’s foreign ministry issued a warning against foreign visitors and diplomats and urged them to leave Kyiv. Merz is expected to renew Germany’s support for Ukraine with a new military aid package worth around €1 billion, in addition to generators, substations and repair kits worth €350 million to strengthen the Ukrainian power grid under attack. Zelenskyy and Merz visited Kyiv’s National Academy of Sciences, which was recently hit by Russian drones in an attack that killed two people and injured seven others and “was deliberate,” the Ukrainian president said on social media. https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-workers-kil.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PFpk Prefer DW on Google An eyewitness said the Izmir blast felt similar to an 'earthquake' Image: Servet Ulku/Anadolu/picture alliance Advertisement An explosion and fire at a factory in western Turkey left 16 workers dead and 13 injured — two of them seriously — President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Monday evening after a Cabinet meeting. The blast took place at the HABAS steel plant in Aliaga, in the port city of Izmir . Officials like the city's governor Suleyman Elban had given reporters lower casualty figures earlier in the day as search and rescue efforts sought to locate people potenitally trapped under rubble. The plant's production line was in the middle of a shift change rather than active production, according to the governor. Only some 200 workers were present instead of the expected 300. An earlier statement from the governor's office said that the blast happened around noon (09:00 GMT) when an overhead crane toppled into a furnace during the casting of liquid steel. It also said that the authorities were investigating the incident. Izmir mayor fears death toll could rise Mayor Cemil Tugay wrote on X that the initial fire following the blast had been extinguished, but the exact number of dead and injured would become clear only after the debris had been cleared. Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci, announced that those injured in the incident were taken to hospital and their condition was being closely monitored. The governor's office said search and rescue efforts were underway Image: Kadir Özen/DHA Minister of Justice Akın Gürlek said that four public prosecutors had been assigned to the case. 'I thought it was an earthquake' Eyewitness Nuri Ali Ulker described the blast as "very intense." "The ground shook," he was quoted as saying by the state-run Anadolu news agency. Another witness, Deniz Ulker, told the agency that the explosion "felt like the earth's crust was shifting beneath us. I thought it was an earthquake." Turkey's big bet to become the new energy hub To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The HABAS plant was established in 1987 and can produce 4.5 million tons of steel annually, according to the company's website. Leftist opposition lashes out at the government Turkey's leftist opposition party TIP lashed out at the government saying that the blast once again laid bare how occupational health and safety were completely disregarded in the country. The described the incident as "workplace homicide." In an online post, TIP leader Erkan Bas said that "[t]he regime of bosses has declared war on the workers." Union leader Basaran Aksu said that "the massacre calls for the resignation of the minister of labor." He alleged that "workers' blood" was being shed for profit. According to the Health and Safety Labor Watch, an independent NGO in Turkey, there were 226 workplace deaths reported across the country in September this year. For orientation, that is around two-thirds of the total that Germany — with a very similar total population — recorded in an entire year in 2025.
